title: Gradient of a Displacement-Time Graph
page_title: Gradient of a Displacement-Time Graph | Cambridge (CIE) AS Physics Revision Notes 2023

blocks.md:
- Displacement-time graphs show the changing position of an object in motion
- They also show the direction an object is moving with respect to its starting position

  - A **positive **gradient on a displacement-time graph shows a constant velocity in the **positive **direction
  - A **negative** gradient on a displacement-time graph shows a constant velocity in the **negative** direction
- The gradient (slope) of a displacement-time graph is equal to the **velocity**

  - The **steeper **the slope, the **greater** the velocity

blocks.label: Worked Example
blocks.md:
A car driver sees a hazard ahead and applies the brakes to bring the car to a stop.

![WE - S-T gradient question image, downloadable AS & A Level Physics revision notes](assets/3cfa23bf2fd5-2-1-4-we-s-t-gradient-question-image.png)

What does the displacement-time graph look like?

**Answer:**

- When the velocity-time graph is a horizontal line, this means constant velocity

  - This is a straight, diagonal line on a displacement-time graph
- When the velocity-time graph is a diagonal line towards the negative direction, this means decreasing velocity (deceleration)

  - This is a curve with a decreasing gradient on a displacement-time graph

![Paired displacement–time and velocity–time graphs show that velocity equals the gradient: displacement rises linearly to t1, then curves to t2 as its gradient decreases; velocity is constant to t1, then falls linearly to zero at t2.](assets/459e247cc6b8-8b47c369df069452-updated-new-2-1-4-we-s-t-gradie.png)

blocks.label: Exam Hint
blocks.md: Don’t forget that velocity is a vector quantity; it has a size and a direction. If velocity is initially positive and then becomes negative, then the object has changed direction.
